questions.question: Distinguish between an element, a compound and a molecule, giving one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: An element contains only one kind of atom (e.g. iron, Fe, or oxygen, O2). A compound contains two or more different elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio (e.g. water, H2O, or sodium chloride, NaCl). A molecule is two or more atoms chemically bonded together, which may be of the same element (O2) or different elements (H2O, CO2).

questions.question: State the number of atoms of each element and the total number of atoms in Ca(OH)2 and in H2SO4.
questions.expected_answer: Ca(OH)2: calcium 1, oxygen 2, hydrogen 2; total 5 atoms. H2SO4: hydrogen 2, sulfur 1, oxygen 4; total 7 atoms.

questions.question: Explain why H2O and H2O2 are different substances and what this means for writing formulas.
questions.expected_answer: A formula records the fixed ratio of atoms in a compound. H2O has hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio 2 to 1 (water), while H2O2 has them in the ratio 1 to 1 (hydrogen peroxide), so they are different compounds with different properties. Therefore the subscripts in a formula must never be changed, for example when balancing an equation, because that would describe a different substance.
